purpose: Repair the ONE blocking finding of c2-plan-stage-schema.v7.review-independent.json, IR-C2V7-01, and the ten non-blocking findings recorded with it. v7 is very nearly right and is NOT rewritten: the duplicate-key repair held in both directions under direct attack, a hunt of the whole bytes-versus-parse class found nothing outside the two declared lists, the 139-row matrix ran to termination with zero escapes and zero COUNTER-ONLY rows, and an independent sweep of 164 candidate mutations admitted none. All of that is preserved. What failed is one level ABOVE all of it: the totality that decides which leaves are under the primitive was itself written as a list of JSON types -- an integer walker and a number walker -- so a BOOLEAN leaf was enumerated by neither, and one byte flipping this lane's own claim to have reproduced IR-C2V6-01 reached exit 0 under a banner still reading 'with no unbound bucket'. The repair is not a boolean walker. The candidate totality now names no scalar type at all: it names the two CONTAINER cases and lets every other JSON type fall through to a leaf, the type coverage is MEASURED against the RFC 8259 value space rather than declared, a leaf whose type has no disposition rule is a named finding, and the PATH and JSON TYPE of every node of this document are bound by one digest so that a type whose value is genuinely narrative still cannot be added, renamed or retyped silently.

resolves.IR-C2V5-01: REPAIRED. The vector itself is retained as a live L6c case executed against the pinned v5 bytes on every run.
resolves.IR-C2V5-02: REPAIRED. v5 declared five type gates, broke two, and three could be stripped with zero findings. v8 declares its gates as the primitive's own entry points and L7 breaks EVERY one of them, each row asserting a specific finding id and the subject under test.
resolves.IR-C2V5-03: REPAIRED. L2c binds every integer leaf AND every JSON number leaf of THIS document to a value this run measured or to a byte of a hash-verified pinned input, with no unbound bucket: a leaf nobody binds is itself a named finding, so narrowing the binding table fails closed. retainedFalseAcceptVectors.measuredThisRun and theDefect.wholeDocumentSweep are inside the binding, not exempt from it, and every one of those leaves is probed with hostile spellings and arbitrary value drift on every run.
resolves.IR-C2V5-04: REPAIRED. L7 breaks every layer as well as every gate, including the anchor functions v5 left unbroken, and each break is re-run against a candidate whose every bound counter has been republished from the mutant's own measurements. A row whose finding survives only before republication is reported as COUNTER-ONLY and fails the suite, so no counter can be the sole detector of any break.
resolves.IR-C2V6-01: REPAIRED. main() did `candidate = json.loads(path.read_text())` with no object_pairs_hook. CPython keeps the LAST occurrence of a duplicated key, so inserting `  "version": 6.0,` immediately before the existing `  "version": 6,` produced a parsed object byte-for-byte identical to the parse of the unedited file: exit 0, full green banner, including the line certifying 105 integer leaves of THIS document bound with no unbound bucket, over a document of record carrying a float at the one key an explicit named rule requires to be a JSON integer. Four things change. The parse itself becomes a primitive gate, jx_loads, which returns the parse AND an explicit account of what the host threw away, and it covers duplicate keys at any depth, the non-RFC constants NaN and Infinity, and number tokens whose spelling is not the canonical spelling of their value. EVERY JSON input this checker loads goes through it, not only the candidate. A structural scan of this file's own syntax tree requires every json.load and json.loads call to pass an object_pairs_hook, with two named, counted exemptions that exist to reproduce the predecessor's own parse as evidence, so the property is over the whole tree instead of over a list of inputs somebody remembered. And the sha256 of the exact candidate bytes that were parsed is computed from those bytes and printed in the banner, so the verdict names the document it is a verdict about. The vector is retained as executable: the mechanism runs on every invocation as L8 against three pinned documents, and the full execution of the pinned, REJECTED check-c2-v6.py over the eighteen-byte edit is a retained --selftest row that must still find it FULLY GREEN.
resolves.IR-C2V7-01: REPAIRED. check-c2-v7.py built its candidate totality from _integer_leaf_steps and _number_leaf_steps. jx_type decides boolean BEFORE integer -- correctly, and that is the primitive's central virtue -- so a boolean leaf was enumerated by neither walker, never entered candidate_bindings, and never reached the unbound-bucket check. Changing theParseDefect/minimalReproduction/reproducedByThisLane from true to false, one token and ONE BYTE with no source modification, produced exit 0 and a full green banner over a document of record stating that this lane did NOT reproduce the single finding v7 existed to discharge. The same flip worked at the IR-C2V4-01 twin, and a new boolean leaf at the root or at depth was admitted likewise, while the identical injected leaf spelled 17, 17.0, NaN or 1E2 was refused by name. Five things change and none of them is a new walker. _number_leaf_steps is DELETED. The totality is jx_leaf_census, which names the two container cases and lets every other JSON type fall through to a leaf, so its type coverage is generated by the data model rather than enumerated by an author. jx_type_space MEASURES, over a witness corpus required to realise every member of JX_TYPES, which types the census reports as leaves and which it descends through, and requires JX_TYPES to be exactly the RFC 8259 value space under one declared refinement of number into integer and number. LEAF_TYPE_RULES is required to EQUAL that measurement rather than to assert its own coverage, and a leaf whose JSON type has no rule is a named C2V8-LEAFRULE finding rather than a silent pass. The two reproducedByThisLane leaves are bound to what this run actually measured about each reproduction. And the PATH and JSON TYPE of every node of this document, container nodes included, are hashed into one digest published here and bound to what the run measures, so a string leaf, a null leaf or an EMPTY array or object -- which holds no leaf for any census to reach -- cannot be added, removed, renamed or retyped without a named finding. The vector is retained as executable: L6d executes the pinned check-c2-v7.py's own enumeration over eight vectors on every invocation, and the full execution of the pinned, REJECTED check-c2-v7.py over the one-byte edit is a retained --selftest row that must still find it FULLY GREEN.
resolves.IR-C2V7-02: REPAIRED. the duplicate-path walk was RECURSIVE and recursed only when a duplicate had actually been recorded, so a duplicate key nested beyond about a thousand objects produced an uncaught RecursionError -- full traceback, exit 1, ZERO findings -- on exactly and only the vector the gate exists to catch, while the same document WITHOUT a duplicate was handled gracefully by a sibling guard that converts the same exception into a named finding. The banner claimed 'every duplicate key at any depth'. The walk is iterative now, and so are jx_walk and jx_leaf_census; the claim is EXECUTED at a declared depth on every run by parse_depth_probe, with a control at the same depth, and the depth is published and bound rather than left as the word 'any'. What remains bounded is jx_canon, which is recursive over a VALUE and is never applied to a whole candidate document; that is RES-C2V8-13 with its own measured number.

theParseDefect.summary: check-c2-v6.py main() reads the candidate with `json.loads(path.read_text())` and no object_pairs_hook. theEnumerationDefect.summary: check-c2-v7.py's candidate totality was built from two walkers, _integer_leaf_steps and _number_leaf_steps, each of which named the JSON type it covered. A boolean leaf is enumerated by neither. It therefore never entered the binding table, never reached the unbound-bucket check, and no layer bound its value. The document held exactly two boolean leaves and both were this lane's own claims to have reproduced the defects it discharges. It is not a defect in the primitive: jx_type(True) is 'boolean' and jx_int(True) is False, and both of those are CORRECT and are what make the primitive sound. The defect is that the enumeration was written over two of the seven JSON types, which is why no amount of strengthening the comparison closes it.
theEnumerationDefect.thePattern: This is the third consecutive version whose retained residual pointed exactly one JSON type away from the live hazard. v5's pointed at gate dominance while the live hazard was the taint model; v6's blind spot named strings while the live hazard was floats; v7's RES-C2V7-07 names strings while the live hazard is booleans. The cause is structural and not editorial: a totality that enumerates WHICH TYPES IT COVERS is a list of places, and the defect moves to a place not on the list. That is the failure v6 was authored to escape at the COMPARISON layer, where it stopped patching operators and built a primitive; it reappeared at the ENUMERATION layer. The repair is therefore not a boolean walker, because a boolean walker would leave the same structure in place with one more entry in it.

thePrimitive.why: Every repair before v6 guarded call sites. v4 guarded the wire validator and left its census bare; v5 guarded the census and left its own repro enumeration bare. Each repair was a list of places and the defect moved to a place not on the list. v6 fixed that and built the primitive - and the defect moved BELOW it, to the parser, which is not a place on any list either and is the one boundary every layer inherits without choosing to. v8 keeps v6's design entirely and adds the parse to the primitive.
thePrimitive.whatItIs: jx_canon, a total, length-framed, type-tagged canonical encoding of a JSON value, and everything else defined in terms of it. Comparison, ordering, membership, key lookup, set algebra, dedup, sorting and extremes are all decided by STRING equality or STRING ordering over canonical tokens. v8 adds jx_loads, the PARSE, to the same block: the boundary at which the bytes become a value is a law-18 gate like any other, and an adopter who copies the block gets it rather than having to remember it.
thePrimitive.whyItIsSoundAndNotJustCareful: jx_canon is INVERTIBLE. jx_decanon reconstructs the original value exactly, type and all, which means jx_canon is injective, which means it can never give two distinct JSON values the same token. That is executed over the whole corpus on every run and the counts are published: corpus values, distinct tokens and round trips must all agree.
thePrimitive.theOperatorSpace: Equality, inequality and their operator.* call forms; ordering in both directions and their call forms; membership and non-membership over lists, tuples, sets and dict keys; key lookup by subscript, get, pop, setdefault and fromkeys; set algebra including subset, superset, disjointness, union, intersection and difference; dedup through set(), frozenset(), set literals and set and dict comprehensions; aggregation through sorted, min, max, sum and Counter; container equality at any depth, where [1] equals [1.0] and an object with an integer value equals the same object with the float; boolean-as-integer, where hash(True) equals hash(1); signed zero; foreign numeric types that compare equal to an integer; BARE TRUTHINESS, where bool(1), bool(1.0) and bool(True) are all the same value so `if x:` carries exactly the equivalence semantics this table exists to enumerate; %d STRINGIFICATION; and THE PARSE, where json.loads keeps the last duplicate key, accepts NaN and Infinity, and turns `-0` into 0 and `1E2` into 100.0. The last three groups are v8's: the truthiness and stringification rows were omitted from v6's table, which called itself the operator space, and the parse rows are IR-C2V6-01. Every row carries a live demonstration that the host-language hazard still reproduces AND a demonstration that the primitive answers differently, and both are executed on every run.
thePrimitive.whyTheContainerHalfMatters: hash(1), hash(1.0) and hash(True) are equal, so len({1, 1.0, True}) is 1. Three distinct JSON values silently become one, and a cardinality published from that set is a false measurement that no equality guard would ever see. This is why the repair could not be a wider list of comparison operators.
thePrimitive.shouldACheckerCompareAMeasuredValueAgain: The comparison exists to catch contract drift and it is also what creates the false-accept surface. v8 keeps the comparison and removes the surface: jx_bind asserts the JSON type of each side independently and FIRST, then compares canonical strings. No numeric operator runs, so there is no coercion path to defend. The residual risk is no longer numeric; it is that the measurement function measures the wrong space, which is RES-C2V6-04 and is a different failure mode.
thePrimitive.whatThePrimitiveCannotDo: It canonicalises a value it is GIVEN, and v8 moves the boundary of that sentence rather than repeating it. The host language collapses equal-hashing dict keys at CONSTRUCTION: the object literal mapping 1, true and 1.0 to three different values is already a one-entry object by the time any gate runs. jx_keyset and jx_unique close that for sequences, and a JSON parse cannot produce it because object keys are always strings - which v6 stated correctly, and which was one word away from IR-C2V6-01, because the NEIGHBOURING construction-time loss is duplicate keys and that one IS reachable from a parse. jx_loads closes it. What remains is an internally built map that loses information upstream of the gate, which is measured and declared rather than mitigated.
thePrimitive.portability: The primitive is delimited in the source by BEGIN and END markers and the delimited region is verified on every run to have no free name outside its declared portability boundary, so it can be copied into another checker verbatim. That is a coverage claim and is held to the same standard as any other: the count is measured and published as primitiveFreeNamesOutsideTheBoundary. STATED PRECISELY, BECAUSE v7 STATED IT LOOSELY: what the region gives an adopter is AVAILABILITY. jx_loads, jx_leaf_census, jx_type_space and jx_bind_value are inside it, so an adopter cannot fail to receive them; json_load_sites, json_parse_evasion_sites and parse_scan_findings -- the things that make USING the parse gate structural -- are OUTSIDE it, at module scope, so an adopter who copies only the region gets the parse gate and nothing that requires it. PARSE EVERY JSON INPUT WITH jx_loads, not only the one you call the candidate, and emit a named finding at the position for every problem it reports. COPY jx_leaf_census AND jx_type_space AND USE THEM FOR ANY TOTALITY OVER A DOCUMENT. Do not write a walker per JSON type. Then use jx_bind_value, which is total over the JSON scalar space, wherever a totality does the binding: jx_bind and jx_bind_text are specialised, and a totality built on a specialised binding is only as wide as the specialisations somebody wrote. This step is IR-C2V7-01.

Replace every wire-touching equality, inequality, ordering, membership and subset with the jx equivalent; replace subscript and get on wire keys with jx_get or jx_at; replace set() and set literals over wire values with jx_keyset or jx_unique.

Replace sorted over wire values with jx_sorted, WHICH ORDERS A HETEROGENEOUS JSON TYPE SET BY CANONICAL TOKEN AND DOES NOT REFUSE ONE, or with jx_sorted_homogeneous, which refuses it by name. thePrimitive.theParseIsAGateToo: IR-C2V6-01. json.loads is not injective over bytes. jx_loads returns (value, problems): it repairs nothing and guesses nothing, it hands back the parse the host produced next to an explicit account of what the host threw away, and a caller that discards the account is visible in the caller's own source rather than invisible in the parser's. check-trusted-request-context-v3.py in this same directory already refuses duplicate keys by RAISING from an object_pairs_hook and retains a scored selftest row for it; v8 reports instead of raising, so the refusal is a NAMED FINDING AT THE POSITION and not an exit code, because a non-zero exit is not evidence a guard fired.
thePrimitive.orderingAndEqualityAgree: v6's jx_order reported EQUAL for 0.0 against -0.0 and for NaN against every float, both of which jx_equal calls distinct, and v6 disclosed only the equality half of that divergence. v8 does not disclose the ordering half; it removes it. jx_order decides the equal case by the same canonical string comparison jx_equal uses, before any < runs, and returns None - not comparable - for two distinct values of the same JSON type that do not order, which after this change is NaN and only NaN. thePrimitive.howToStateTheNumericPropertyCorrectly: STATED ACCURATELY BECAUSE BOTH v6 DOCUMENTS STATED IT WRONGLY. v6 claimed 'no numeric operator is ever executed on a wire operand'. That is false as worded: jx_order runs `a < b` and jx_int_in_range runs `low <= value <= high`. The property that is true, and that is the one doing the work, is that NO COMPARISON BETWEEN OPERANDS OF DIFFERENT JSON TYPE IS EVER EXECUTED. Both of those functions gate every operand to the same JSON type FIRST, so no coercion path is reachable; `<` between two values already proved to be JSON integers cannot coerce anything. Equality never runs a numeric operator at all - it is string equality over canonical tokens.
thePrimitive.whatTheAdoptionStepsUsedToSayAndWhyThatM: v6's step 3 told an adopter to call jx_min and jx_max, NEITHER OF WHICH EXISTED anywhere in check-c2-v6.py, so following the normative instructions verbatim produced a NameError; and both v6 documents attributed to jx_sorted a refusal of heterogeneous JSON type sets that it does not perform - it orders them, and jx_sorted_homogeneous is the function that refuses. thePrimitive.theEnumerationIsAGateToo: IR-C2V7-01. The primitive decides whether two values are comparable and whether they are equal. It cannot decide WHICH VALUES ARE PUT TO IT, and in v7 that decision was made by two hand-written walkers that named the JSON types they covered. v8MeasuredCountersRule: EVERY LEAF OF THIS DOCUMENT IS UNDER THREE OBLIGATIONS AT ONCE, and the first of them names no JSON type. POPULATION: the per-type leaf counts are published and bound. residuals.title: the TEXT of a narrative string leaf is unbound, and the size of that is a measured number

residuals.title: bare truthiness is measured and published, not guarded
residuals.detail: bool(1), bool(1.0) and bool(True) are the same value, so `if x:` on a wire number carries exactly the int/float/bool equivalence semantics the operator space exists to enumerate. v6's 28-row table omitted it and L4's _hazard_pairs does not treat ast.If, ast.While, ast.IfExp, ast.BoolOp, ast.Assert, unary not or comprehension-ifs as comparison sites. v8 adds the operator-space rows and measures the sites over real source, publishing and BINDING the counts for this file and for the pinned check-c2-v6.py -- but it does not make them findings. residuals.title: L8's structural parse scan is SYNTACTIC, and what actually held the exemption line was the counter binding
residuals.detail: json_load_sites matches an ast.Call whose func is an Attribute or a Name spelled load or loads. The v7 reviewer measured six mutated syntax trees against it: a bare json.loads added inside a declared-exempt function, one hidden among the hazard demonstrations, and a no-op object_pairs_hook=dict were all invisible TO THE SCAN and were refused only because every parse counter is published and bound, so each moved a counter and became a named C2V7-CANDIDATE finding; and json.JSONDecoder().decode and getattr(json, 'loads') were invisible to BOTH, changing no counter at all. The exemption list genuinely could not be widened silently, and it was the counter binding that refused it, not the scan that is described as making the property structural. v8 counts the two decoder evasions and requires them to be zero -- which is what L4 already did for its own analogous evasions and what L8 did not -- and publishes the count as parseEvasionSites. The measured boundary: the scan sees TWO syntactic shapes and the evasion counter sees TWO more; a parse reached through a name this file computes at run time is outside all four. parseEvasionSites is published and bound, the detector is probed against a tree that plainly carries both shapes so a count of zero is distinguishable from a detector that sees nothing, and the full parse-site decomposition -- parseHookedLoadSites plus parseDeclaredHazardSites plus parseDeclaredPredecessorParses plus parseUngatedLoadSites equals parseJsonLoadSites -- is itself a finding when it does not hold.
residuals.whyNotClosed: Following a run-time-computed name to a parse needs a data-flow analysis over Python, which is the same instrument RES-C2V8-01 declines to build for gate dominance and would itself need review. Carrying it unbuilt would be a paper seal.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the counter binding, which is what the reviewer measured actually holding the line and which is now DISCLOSED as doing so rather than implied to be the scan's work; the evasion counter, which closes the two shapes that moved no counter at all; L4's own eval/exec/getattr-dispatch counters over the same tree; and the fact that a parse reached that way still has to survive every layer that reads the parsed object.

residuals.title: 'at any depth' is now a measured depth, and jx_canon is still recursive
residuals.detail: IR-C2V7-02: v7's the duplicate-path walk was recursive and recursed only when a duplicate had actually been recorded, so past the host recursion limit of 1000 the one vector L8 exists to catch produced an uncaught RecursionError -- traceback, exit 1, ZERO findings -- while the same document without a duplicate was converted into a named finding by a sibling guard. the duplicate-path walk, jx_walk and jx_leaf_census are all iterative now and the duplicate-key claim is EXECUTED at the depth published as parseDepthProbeDepth on every run, with a control at the same depth. What remains recursive is jx_canon, which walks a VALUE rather than a document and is never applied to a whole candidate; the deepest value it is applied to in this checker is the v4-identity projection and the leaf-and-type skeleton, both of which are two levels deep by construction. The measured boundary: the duplicate-key claim is executed to the published depth and is untested beyond it; the host json.loads C scanner accepts far deeper input than that, so 'any depth' is bounded by this probe's declared number and not by the parser. The depth at which the claim is executed is published and bound as parseDepthProbeDepth, with a control at the same depth, and the number of times the duplicate is named at its full path is published as parseDepthNamedAtThePosition.
residuals.whyNotClosed: Making jx_canon iterative would rewrite the single decision point every other layer stands on, to remove a limit no input in this corpus approaches, in the version whose blocking finding is about that decision point's INPUT SET rather than its implementation. Rewriting closed code for an unreached hazard is how a repair becomes a rewrite.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the iterative walks, which are what the duplicate-key claim actually depends on; the depth probe, which executes the claim rather than asserting it; MALFORMED_SHAPE_EXCEPTIONS, which already carries RecursionError so that a deep traversal inside check() becomes a named C2V8-TOTALITY finding rather than a traceback; and the load-time refusal, which converts the same exception on a pinned input into a distinct exit code.

residuals.title: the number-token scanner has one measured false positive
residuals.detail: jx_number_tokens starts a token at '-' and stops at the first character outside the number class, so jx_loads('{"a": -Infinity}') returns TWO problems: the correct non-rfc-constant for -Infinity and a spurious number-text problem for the bare token '-'. The v7 reviewer audited the scanner hard and found nothing else: over the candidate it finds every numeric leaf with 0 false positives and 0 false negatives, a 4000-case randomised differential fuzz over documents containing framing-lookalike strings, escaped quotes and exponent-shaped keys found 0 failures, and nineteen hand-built adversarial tokens including 1e309, 2e308, 1e-400, 0e0, 1.0e0, -0.0, 1e+16 and a sixteen-digit integer were all classified correctly. The measured boundary is therefore exactly one input shape, it produces one extra finding and never one fewer, and any document carrying it is refused anyway by C2V8-NONRFC.
residuals.whyNotClosed: The scanner is fuzz-verified at its current digest and the v7 review graded this MINOR after measuring that it errs only towards refusing. Editing a fuzz-verified instrument to remove a finding it emits in the safe direction, in the version whose blocking finding is elsewhere, would trade a measured property for an unmeasured one.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the direction of the error, which is towards refusal and never towards admission; C2V8-NONRFC, which refuses the same document by name; and the published pinned-input token census, which measures the scanner over every pinned JSON input on every run.

residuals.title: the type space is anchored to a DECLARED table of the standard's productions, and that one table is not executable
residuals.detail: THIS IS THE SHARPEST ATTACK ON THE IR-C2V7-01 REPAIR AND IT IS WRITTEN HERE RATHER THAN LEFT FOR A REVIEWER TO FIND. The totality itself names no JSON type: jx_leaf_census names the two container cases and lets everything else fall through, so it cannot be narrower than the set of types a document can hold. But the DISPOSITION of a leaf is looked up in LEAF_TYPE_RULES, which is a seven-row table, and that table's completeness is established by comparison against JX_TYPES and JX_RFC8259_PRODUCTIONS, which are also declared tables. Four of the five links in that chain are EXECUTED and measured on every run: LEAF_TYPE_RULES must equal the leaf/container split jx_type_space MEASURES by running the census over witnesses; every member of JX_TYPES must be realised by a witness; every member must refine some declared production; every production must refine into declared types; and no type may be both a leaf and a container. The link that is NOT executable is the last one: that RFC 8259 sections 3 to 7 define exactly seven value productions and no eighth. That sentence is read from the standard by a human and transcribed into JX_RFC8259_PRODUCTIONS. MEASURED BOUNDARY: primitiveTypeSpaceRfcProductions productions, one declared refinement (number into integer and number), primitiveTypeSpaceWitnesses witnesses, primitiveTypeSpaceDeclaredTypes declared types of which primitiveTypeSpaceUnwitnessedTypes are unwitnessed, and primitiveTypeSpaceAdmissions types that are neither a leaf nor a container. Every one of those is published and bound. The unexecutable link is exactly one transcription of one sentence of one standard.
residuals.whyNotClosed: A checker cannot execute a standards document. The alternatives are worse rather than better: deriving the production set from the host parser would anchor the type space to CPython's json module, which is the very thing IR-C2V6-01 showed is not a trustworthy authority about JSON; and deriving it from the type space would be circular. What can be done is to make every OTHER link executable, publish the figures, and say plainly which single link is not - which is what this residual does. Naming it is not closing it.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the fall-through construction of jx_leaf_census, which does not consult any of these tables and reports a leaf of ANY type including one no table names; the C2V8-LEAFRULE finding, which fires on a leaf whose type carries no disposition rule, so an unanticipated type is a named finding rather than a silent pass even if every table above is wrong about it; and the live injection probe, which puts a witness of every declared type into the candidate at unbound paths on every run and requires each to be named.

residuals.title: the live injection probe is exhaustive over the TYPE SPACE and sampled over PATHS
residuals.detail: The value ledger is exhaustive over PATHS: every leaf of this document is reached by jx_leaf_census and disposed of, and candidateLeaves is bound to what the walk finds. The ORACLE for that ledger - the probe that shows an unbound leaf really does become a named finding - is exhaustive over the type space and sampled over paths: it injects a witness of every one of candidateTotalityTypes JSON types at each of four declared target paths, the document root and three blocks at depth, for candidateTotalityCases executed cases. MEASURED BOUNDARY: four target paths out of candidateContainers container nodes in this document. A ledger that named leaves correctly at those four positions and nowhere else would satisfy the probe; nothing measures the other container nodes.
residuals.whyNotClosed: Injecting a witness of every JSON type at every container node of this document would be candidateContainers times candidateTotalityTypes times the witness count recomputations of the whole ledger on every ordinary invocation, which is a cost this checker cannot carry and still be run routinely - and the cost model is the reason the predecessor sweep is the expensive layer rather than this one. Sampling and saying so is honest; sampling and calling it exhaustive is the defect this lineage exists to close.
residuals.whatStandsInFrontOfIt: the ledger's own path-exhaustiveness, which is structural rather than probed: the disposition loop runs over jx_leaf_census output and has no path table to be wrong about; the skeleton digest, which binds the path and JSON type of all candidateNodes nodes; and L7, which breaks the ledger itself and requires the probe to report the break.

L9 could not see it, because the wrong name occurs legitimately many times elsewhere in that document; that is the class RES-C2V8-10 concedes L9 does not close, and this is the one position where it was live.
